summary.headline: R R Kabel Q2 FY27 revenue rose 52% to INR 3,284 crores and PAT 55% to INR 181 crores, with H1 the highest ever.
summary.overview: R R Kabel reported record half-year revenue, operating EBITDA and PAT for H1 FY27, with consolidated revenue up 53% and PAT up 87%. Q2 EBITDA margin expanded about 60 bps to 8.7%, while wires and cables margins improved and FMEG remained loss-making in the seasonally weak quarter. Management declared an interim dividend of INR 6.50 per share, approved INR 200 crores for Rajasthan land, and signed a deal on 25 September 2026 to acquire UM Cables' optical fibre business for about INR 77 crores (not yet recognised). Management trimmed FY27 wires and cables volume growth guidance to about 14-15% from 16-18%.

segments.name: Wires and cables
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR 3,010 crores (+53%) and segment margin 9.4%; H1 revenue INR 5,890 crores (+55%) and margin 9.6%. Volumes grew high single digit in Q2, with wires in double digits and cables in single digits; H1 volume growth was low teens.

segments.name: FMEG
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR 274 crores (+42%), with a loss of about INR 12 crores after breakeven in Q1 FY27. Growth led by appliances and new products; fans, the main category, are seasonally weak in Q2. Full-year segment breakeven target retained.

segments.name: UM Cables optical fibre (pending acquisition)
segments.commentary: Agreed consideration about INR 77 crores, subject to post-closing adjustments and conditions precedent; not yet in results. Management said the plant ran at very low utilisation and no revenue contribution should be assumed for FY27.

guidance_outlook: Wires and cables volume growth for FY27 now about 14-15%, versus earlier 16-18%; management said H2 volumes are expected to be higher year-on-year.
Wires and cables segment EBIT margin target of 9.5% for FY27 and about 10.5% for FY28, unchanged from the three-year plan of roughly 300 bps improvement from FY26.
FMEG expected to reach full-year segment profit breakeven in FY27 after Q2 loss; H2 profitability expected to improve, with fans seen as the key profit driver.
Export share of revenue expected at 30-35% for the rest of FY27.
Working capital days expected to stay in the 45-50 day range.
FY27 capex of INR 550-600 crores on track, plus about INR 100 crores for Rajasthan land in H2 and UM Cables payout separately; FY28 capex around INR 300 crores ("seems okay").
capex_capacity: Capex plan for FY27 remains INR 550-600 crores; about INR 281 crores spent so far in H1 (excludes UM Cables).

INR 200 crores approved for Rajasthan land acquisition as the first step of a new capex plan; major outflow expected this year and remainder in H1 FY28, with detailed capex plan due in one to two quarters.
Roorkee plant relocation underway, with FMEG capacity to be increased; the new site is leased, so limited capex is expected.
Cable capacity additions are driving export growth in cables, per management.
Management said the new Rajasthan capex is for wires and cables growth.
demand_pricing: Management cited higher raw material (metal) prices, which pressured gross margin, with gross margin down about 100 bps; product mix also contributed.
Export growth outpaced domestic in Q2; Europe and Middle East are the largest export regions, with equal growth across continents.
Management said competition is a constant feature of the business and did not quantify any impact; it expects to grow through plant utilisation and sales and marketing.
Receivable days improved from 34 to 32 days per management, with receivables rising in line with volume growth.
Trade payables and LC-backed metal purchases increased; LC utilisation was about INR 1,290 crores per management.
Management said it adds three to four international approvals each year.

qa_highlights.question: Why did cables volume growth lag wires, given new capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 was affected by monsoon-season variation; domestic cables grew in single digits versus double digits for wires, and export growth came mainly from cables.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY27 volume guidance trimmed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the guidance was fine-tuned from 16-18% to about 15% for volatility and did not cite any segment slowdown.

qa_highlights.question: Why did FMEG slip into loss in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited seasonally muted Q2 demand, since fans are low-season, and said H2 is expected to be stronger, with breakeven targeted for the full year.

qa_highlights.question: Why did trade payables and finance costs rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said higher metal prices and better LC-backed trade utilisation drove payables, and higher interest cost is a normal consequence of high raw material prices.

qa_highlights.question: How much debt increase and FY28 capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said debt will rise modestly, with leverage around 0.55x, and that the increase funds the current capex. FY28 capex is about INR 300 crores, with plus or minus variation.

qa_highlights.question: Plans for UM Cables and its revenue contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no bigger revenue contribution should be assumed for FY27 until control of the business is achieved; a detailed business plan is due in about one quarter.

risks_watch: Volume trajectory: H2 needs about mid-teens growth on a high base, and the cables segment is growing more slowly than wires.
Gross margin pressure from high metal prices and rising finance cost from higher LC-backed payables and borrowings.
FMEG Q2 loss: full-year breakeven needs a sharp H2 turnaround, and cumulative losses are about INR 17 crores.
Rising receivables and payables, with working capital reliant on LC-backed trade; FY27 capex and Rajasthan land add to debt.
UM Cables acquisition: plant under-utilised, with no detailed plan until the next quarter; deal not yet completed.
Competitive intensity increasing in domestic wires, per analyst questions; management gave no quantified view.
summary.management_tone: Confident on H1 delivery and margin targets, but more guarded on forward volumes: guidance was trimmed and management declined to comment on FY28 volumes, calling the market volatile. Answers on working capital, debt and UM Cables were brief, with few specifics.
key_quotes: Against this backdrop, I am pleased to share that R R Kabel has delivered its highest ever half yearly revenue, operating EBITDA, and profit after tax.
Overall volume growth was in high single-digits, where wire outpacing cables.
So our margin guidance remains the same. To be specific, 9.5% for this year and approx. 10.5% for FY 2028.
Yes, there will be some increase in debt. See, first of all, if you see even my debt leverage is quite favourable.

adds.what: New Rajasthan wires and cables capacity (land approved INR 200 crore; detailed capex plan pending)
Roorkee FMEG plant relocation with increased FMEG capacity (leased site, limited capex)

growth.why: Management cut FY27 wires and cables volume growth to about 14-15% (from 16-18%) while holding the 9.5% FY27 W&C EBIT margin, with H2 volumes guided higher YoY; backing is partial, as capex of INR 550-600 crore is on track (INR 281 crore spent in H1) and Rajasthan land (INR 200 crore) is approved, but no specific new capacity commissioning dates or order book figures were given.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: W&C segment EBIT margin target held at 9.5% for FY27 and about 10.5% for FY28 (from 9.6% in H1 FY27), though gross margin fell about 100 bps on higher metal prices and FMEG remains loss-making (Q2 loss about INR 12 crores).

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: INR 200 crores approved for Rajasthan land with major outflow this year and remainder in H1 FY28; FY27 capex of INR 550-600 crores on track with INR 281 crores spent in H1, but no commissioning dates were given.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 W&C volume growth guided down to about 14-15% from 16-18%, with H2 volumes expected higher YoY; H1 volume growth was low teens and Q2 high single digit.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management said a detailed capex plan for the new Rajasthan capacity is due in one to two quarters; utilisation was not disclosed, so the trigger rests on the land approval and stated plan.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management trimmed FY27 W&C volume guidance to 14-15% from 16-18%, and the only held guidance is margins and capex.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Volume guidance was already cut, and H2 needs about mid-teens growth on a high base while FMEG needs a sharp H2 turnaround to reach full-year breakeven after a Q2 loss of about INR 12 crores.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: FMEG growth led by appliances and new products (FMEG revenue +42% in Q2 to INR 274 crores), and management adds three to four international approvals each year, but no specific launch dates were given.

rows.label: Export growth via cable capacity
rows.why: Export share guided at 30-35% of revenue for rest of FY27, with export growth in Q2 outpacing domestic and driven mainly by cables, per management.

rows.label: UM Cables optical fibre acquisition
rows.why: Deal signed 25 September 2026 for about INR 77 crores, subject to conditions precedent; plant ran at very low utilisation and management assumes no FY27 revenue contribution, with a business plan due in about one quarter.

tone.note: Management was confident on H1 delivery (PAT +87%) and held the 9.5% FY27 W&C margin and capex plan, but was guarded on volumes after cutting guidance; analysts pushed on cables lagging wires, competition, FMEG Q2 loss, and the UM Cables deal, which got brief answers.
